The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{x}{4}+C),$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\pi <C<\pi ,$ what is the value of $C?$
question.worked_solution:
The parameter $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{x}{4}+C) \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{1}{4}(x+4C))\end{aligned}
$$

From the graph, we see that the graph of secant has been shifted by $\frac{4\pi }{3}$ units to the **left**. Therefore:

$$
4C=\frac{4\pi }{3}\,⟹\,C=\frac{\pi }{3}
$$
